Context
-------
Read .github/copilot-instructions.md first.

This is the beat of the demo where a network-sourced metric causes an
alert, which Alertmanager groups, inhibits and silences, and which lands
as a readable JSON payload on screen.

Objective
---------
Alert rules, Alertmanager routing, and a local webhook sink that replaces
Slack. Everything offline.

Deliverables
------------
- manifests/alert-rules.yaml        PrometheusRule, kube-prometheus-stack CRD
- manifests/alertmanager-config.yaml AlertmanagerConfig, CRD
- manifests/echo-sink-config.yaml   webhook server source ConfigMap
- manifests/echo-sink.yaml          webhook sink Deployment
- manifests/echo-sink-service.yaml  webhook sink Service
- values/kube-prometheus-stack.yaml must reference both CRDs
- docs/alerting-runbook.md          what to show, in what order

The alert rule
--------------
kind: PrometheusRule
labels: { release: kps }   # must match the kube-prometheus-stack selector

One rule, DemoHighErrorRate:
  expr:
    sum(rate(hubble_http_requests_total{reporter="destination",
      http_status_code=~"5.."}[1m]))
    /
    sum(rate(hubble_http_requests_total{reporter="destination"}[1m]))
    > 0.05
  for: 1m
  labels: { severity: warning, pillar: network }
  annotations:
    summary: "5xx above 5% on {{ $labels.destination_workload }}"
    description: "Source: Cilium Hubble. No application instrumentation."

The `for: 1m` is deliberate and pedagogically important — the presenter
walks through Pending -> Firing on screen. Do not shorten it.

Alertmanager
------------
- route: receiver echo, group_by [alertname, namespace],
  group_wait 10s, group_interval 1m, repeat_interval 4h
- receiver echo: webhook to http://echo-sink.demo.svc.cluster.local:8080/alerts
- no receiver that could reach the internet

Echo sink
---------
A minimal container that logs every request body to stdout as pretty JSON.
Use a known small image, pinned by digest. It exists so the presenter can
`kubectl logs -f` it and read the raw payload on the projector.

docs/alerting-runbook.md must cover, in order:
1. Show the rule YAML. Explain `for` as the difference between an alert
   and a notification.
2. Trigger it. Watch Inactive -> Pending -> Firing.
3. Show two alerts grouping into one notification.
4. Create a silence live from the UI, show notifications stop.
5. Show the raw JSON in the echo sink logs.
6. Explain inhibition in one sentence, without demonstrating it unless
   time allows.

Acceptance
----------
Apply the rules with the demo app and load generator running, then force
5xx. Within ~90s a Firing alert appears in Alertmanager, and `kubectl logs
deploy/echo-sink -n demo` shows a well-formed JSON payload. Paste that
payload into docs/alerting-runbook.md as a reference.
